Done. Here's where it landed.

## The Fitter

**Idea (one sentence):** the time is machinery, not type — each digit is an assembly of brass parts (rods with riveted bosses, bent rods, toothed spoked wheels) that the machine's own two claws take apart into a hopper on the minute and fit back together, part by part, leaving the removed parts on show as a thin drawn *plan* until the new ones are seated.

**Disqualifying the obvious:** the sibling `automaton-haiku45` already had "a mechanical arm traces digits with a pen driven by cams", so instead of tracing letterforms the machine *is* the letterforms. Each of the ten digits is a set of rigid brass pieces (1–3 parts); nothing morphs, no glyph is ever drawn, and the wheels' spokes and teeth turn all minute, so the time itself is running machinery.

**Renders** (all in `.claude/skills/oled-clock/out/`, only `sim/designs/automaton-ds.js` touched):
- `automaton-ds.png` — the still
- `automaton-ds-digits.png` — all ten digits at size
- `automaton-ds-turn.png` — sheet across 10:09:58 (nine → zero, plus the tens roll)
- `automaton-ds-hour.png` — sheet across 10:59:58 (flywheel winds up, the whole bench is thrown and caught)
- `automaton-ds.gif`, `automaton-ds-hour.gif` — 50 fps
- `automaton-ds-wear.png` — burn-in map

**check.mjs** (`--design automaton-ds`, full run): **PASS** — 20,160 frames, worst frame 0.83 ms on SPI 10 MHz, 0 over budget, 30.6 % of the glass lit, hottest pixel ~2.0 years to 50 % at full contrast. `node tools/emulator-test.mjs`: 20 passed, 0 failed (untouched). `frame()` is a pure function of the clock: the plan shown is always the digit the clock is *currently* showing, so the face can never read a wrong time and no old/new bookkeeping is needed.

**Honest weakest point:** the composition is still a bench with a row of numerals on it — a machine *panel* more than a scene with depth. Depth is carried only by the two foreground claws and the half-cropped flywheel/ratchet; the bottom band (flywheel, hopper, mainspring, half ratchet) reads as a row of similar-sized objects. That band is what I would rework next. Two smaller ones: `frame()` costs ~2.5 ms warm (cube 0.7, nixie 1.5, scope 3.7 on the same loaded box), just over the ~2 ms brief, and the ten-bowl digits are the cost — the wheels are heavy at 8–10 primitives each.

Two notes: I applied lessons from the earlier kinetic memory — a flag-topped "1" reads as "7" at 1x (it's now a bar with feet) and four digits in a row reads as traditional (the hours now stand on a raised station above the bench, the minutes on the bench below). And `sim/designs/automaton.js` — the base design I was told not to touch — is still broken: it fails to load with `FROG is not defined`, so it is skipped by every tool.
